title: Polymorphism

notes: The list's type is Unit, but each object is a different class.
u.act() runs the real class's act(): that's dynamic dispatch.
For a mixed Object[] we use instanceof with a pattern variable.
`o instanceof String s` checks and casts in one step.
The final else catches anything unexpected (3.5 here).

exercises.title: An enemy wave
exercises.prompt: Enemy, Slime (attack 3, reward 5) and Archer (attack 7, reward 12) are done. Finish Boss(int level): name "Boss L2" for level 2, attack 20 × level, reward 100 × level. In Wave write static int totalAttack(List<Enemy> wave), static int totalReward(List<Enemy> wave), and static String mostDangerous(List<Enemy> wave) (the name of the enemy with the highest attack; the first one wins a tie; "none" if empty). Use polymorphism: no instanceof or getClass.

tests.call: Wave.totalAttack(java.util.List.of(new Slime(), new Archer(), new Slime()))
Wave.mostDangerous(java.util.List.of(new Archer(), new Boss(1), new Slime()))

tests.why: Let each enemy answer for itself: no instanceof.

hints: Boss stores level in a field and calls super("Boss L" + level).
totalAttack: for (Enemy e : wave) total += e.attack();
mostDangerous: only replace the best when e.attack() > best.attack() (strictly bigger keeps the first on a tie).

exercises.title: Sorting the loot
exercises.prompt: Loot is a mix of unrelated classes: Potion (heal), Weapon (name, damage) and Coin (value), held as Object. Using instanceof with pattern variables, write in Items: static String describe(Object item) giving "Potion +20 hp", "Spear 12 dmg", "Coin x5", or "Unknown" for anything else (including null); static int totalCoins(List<Object> loot) adding up coin values; static int bestDamage(List<Object> loot) giving the highest weapon damage, or 0 if there are no weapons.

tests.call: Items.totalCoins(java.util.List.of(new Coin(5), new Potion(3), new Coin(10)))
Items.bestDamage(java.util.List.of(new Weapon("Club", 6), new Coin(1), new Weapon("Axe", 18)))

tests.name: null
tests.hint_if_fail: instanceof is false for null, so a chain of instanceof checks handles it.

tests.why: Use instanceof with a pattern variable.

hints: if (item instanceof Potion p) return "Potion +" + p.heal + " hp";
In the loops: for (Object o : loot) if (o instanceof Coin c) total += c.value;

exercises.title: Clinic payroll
exercises.prompt: Worker and Doctor (a fixed weekly salary) are done. Write Nurse(String name, int hours, double rate): pay is hours × rate, but hours above 40 are paid 1.5 × rate. Write Volunteer(String name): weekly pay is a 500.0 stipend. In Payroll write static double total(List<Worker> staff) and static String highestPaid(List<Worker> staff) (name; first wins a tie; "none" if empty). payslip() is done in Worker.

tests.call: Payroll.total(java.util.List.of(new Nurse("A", 40, 300), new Doctor("B", 30000), new Volunteer("C")))
Payroll.highestPaid(java.util.List.of(new Nurse("A", 40, 300), new Doctor("B", 30000), new Volunteer("C")))

hints: Nurse keeps hours and rate in fields.
int normal = Math.min(hours, 40); int extra = Math.max(0, hours - 40); return normal * rate + extra * rate * 1.5;
total: for (Worker w : staff) sum += w.weeklyPay();

quiz.why: Dynamic dispatch uses the real object's class.

quiz.q: `Enemy e = new Archer();` Can you call an Archer-only method `e.aim()`?
choices: No: the variable's type (Enemy) decides what you may call
quiz.why: The compiler only knows it's an Enemy.

quiz.q: You keep writing `if (e instanceof Slime) ... else if (e instanceof Archer) ...` for your own enemy classes. Better?
choices: Put a method on Enemy and override it in each class

quiz.q: Why does polymorphism make adding a new enemy type easy?
quiz.why: Only the new class is written; callers don't change.

cards.a: At run time Java runs the overriding method of the object's real class.
if (o instanceof Coin c) { use c directly }
Variable type: what you may call. Object type: which code runs.
Mixed types you don't control, or can't add a method to.

explain: Explain polymorphism to a friend using a game loop as the example: what would the code look like without it?
